headword: {表裏一体|ひょうりいったい}
gloss: two sides of the same coin; inseparable

definitions.gloss: two sides of the same coin, inseparable, forming one body
definitions.explanation: Two things that appear opposite or different but are in fact inseparable aspects of the same thing, like the front and back of a single sheet. Used to express that seemingly contradictory qualities are fundamentally connected.

examples.japanese: {自由|じゆう}と{責任|せきにん}は{表裏一体|ひょうりいったい}だ。
examples.english: Freedom and responsibility are two sides of the same coin.

examples.japanese: リスクとリターンは{表裏一体|ひょうりいったい}の{関係|かんけい}にある。
examples.english: Risk and return are inseparably linked.

examples.japanese: {便利|べんり}さと{危険|きけん}さは{表裏一体|ひょうりいったい}であり、テクノロジーの{恩恵|おんけい}を{受|う}けるには、そのリスクも{理解|りかい}しなければならない。
examples.english: Convenience and danger are inseparable, and to enjoy the benefits of technology, one must also understand its risks.

notes:
USAGE:
A four-character compound ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) used to express that two seemingly opposite concepts are fundamentally inseparable. Often followed by だ, の{関係|かんけい}, or である. Very common in essays, editorials, and formal discussions.

ETYMOLOGY:
{表|ひょう} (front/surface) + {裏|り} (back/reverse) + {一体|いったい} (one body). Literally "front and back as one body."

COMMON PATTERNS:
- AとBは{表裏一体|ひょうりいったい}だ: A and B are two sides of the same coin
- {表裏一体|ひょうりいったい}の{関係|かんけい}: an inseparable relationship
- {表裏一体|ひょうりいったい}をなす: to form two sides of the same coin
